ai_show_review.summary: Psychedelic prankster collages and high‑energy acid test vibes
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert is built around experimental sound‑collage interludes that create a dark, off‑beat psychedelic atmosphere. Energy stays elevated throughout, highlighted by two standout prankster pieces. A good‑quality soundboard capture preserves the quirky details while another source offers only fair clarity.
ai_show_review.review: October 2, 1966 at the Commons of S.F. State College finds the Dead deep in their Acid Test phase, turning the stage into a playground for strange sonic experiments. The set is punctuated by two eerie prankster sound‑collages – one an early “techno” sketch and the other a haunting piano‑driven piece – that give the evening its distinctive, creepy edge. Beyond the collages the band rides a high‑energy current, delivering a performance that feels both playful and unsettling, as if they were deliberately pushing the limits of what a rock concert could be. While the exact song list is lost to history, the available recordings capture enough of the ambience to make this show a fascinating snapshot of the Dead’s early avant‑garde explorations.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with good clarity that reveals the experimental collages and overall performance detail
